note_title: Dollar at a one-year high, oil up 60%: retail stocks likely fall 9% by late January
note_lines: The call: over the next three months the retail-stock fund XRT likely falls about 9%, to $80. Nine times since 2008 the dollar sat at a one-year high while oil was up 30%+ on the year; retailers fell in eight of the nine (median -11%) and lagged the S&P 500 in all nine.
Buy: XRT ATM puts, Feb 19 expiry. Sell short: N/A. Size 10 of 100; the premium is the most it can lose.
Expected return: 8.6% on XRT over 3 months (the median of the eight past cases that share today's gasoline state). Annualized pace about 34% against the 20% bar.
What kills it: an XRT close above $91.06 (4.3% above entry), or oil dropping below +30% on the year / the dollar leaving the top quarter of its one-year range (the critical review conditions).

The other side: nine cases is thin and the three biggest falls were recessions; consumer confidence just jumped 7.5 points; XRT is 400% of its float sold short, so a squeeze on a strong Amazon print is the risk; the holiday season is usually good for retail stocks.
